review_notes: Source-first principal-family decision: the paper’s central contribution is a large-sample test of the debt-covenant hypothesis using covenant-slack distributions for the current-ratio and net-worth covenant samples. The authors state (physical PDF p. 18): “We present our main results in a series of histograms that document the empirical distributions of covenant slack over loan life.” Their primary smoothness test compares expected and observed bin counts around zero (p. 19); the randomization-based robustness test uses the ratio of observations in bin 0 to bin −1 and shuffles covenant thresholds against accounting realizations (p. 27). These are distributional and randomization tests, not fitted regression equations.

The rest of the paper does not supply an eligible regression for this selected family: Table 3 reports Spearman rank correlations (p. 17); Table 5 reports violation frequencies (p. 29); Table 6 compares sample medians across loan-quarter groups (pp. 30–31). Covenant slack is computed as actual covenant-variable realization minus the threshold (p. 15), a deterministic difference, not a regression. Therefore models=[] with status no_baseline_regression is retained.

The family covers both current-ratio and net-worth covenant samples and the paper’s main full and follow-up histogram partitions. The assigned sample record is the current-ratio histogram sample (sample_id current_ratio_covenant), while the source also reports the parallel net-worth covenant sample; neither contains a fitted regression.
descriptive_reason: No baseline regression models are selected in the frozen specification or inventory, so no model-related descriptive statistics apply to this enrichment. The paper’s primary results are covenant-slack distributions/histograms, Spearman correlations, randomization tests, violation frequencies and medians (source pages 15–18 and 27–31), outside the frozen regression-results family.
results_review_notes: Source pages 15–18 and 27–32 were read, and original PDF pages 15, 17–18 and 27–32 were rendered and viewed before opening the matching prior.

The paper describes its main debt-covenant results as distributions/histograms and randomization tests (pp. 18, 27–28). Tables 3–6 report correlations, randomization quantiles/p-values, violation counts, and loan-quarter medians, not baseline regression coefficient fits.

The matching prior has no models or descriptive groups and is consistent with the literal assigned base/inventory. No coefficient cells, model roles, omission reasons, or model-linked descriptive rows are retained.
